17.symbols: $t$, $u$, $t_j$, $\Delta t$: time, kernel lag, jth spike time, fitted neural lead (s); $j$: spike index; $E$, $E_T$, $x=E-E_T$, $\widehat E$: eye angle, fitted threshold angle, angle offset, predicted eye angle (degrees); $f$: firing rate (spikes/s); $k$: position coefficient (spikes/(s degree)); $r$: velocity coefficient (spikes/degree), not a firing rate; $m$: acceleration coefficient (spikes s/degree); $p$: Laplace frequency (1/s); $\tau_+$, $\tau_-$: distinct positive slow/fast response decay times (s); $h_0$, $h$: causal position impulse response before/after delay (degrees/spike), zero at negative effective lag. Dots differentiate time; $h$ is a filter here, not spatial input.

18.symbols: $i$: motor-neuron index; $N_m$: number of contributing ocular motoneurons (count); $R_i$: Pearson correlation between cell $i$'s predicted displacement and measured displacement over the same 350 ms intervals (dimensionless); $R$: the same correlation when the cell index is omitted; angle brackets: motor-population mean; a representative sample estimates it with sampling uncertainty; $R_i^2$: fraction of displacement variance explained after best linear rescaling (dimensionless). Standardized predictors and measured displacement have zero mean and unit variance.

19.symbols: $X$: displacement predicted from one cell's spikes; $Y$: measured eye displacement; $C$: shared upstream contribution to displacement; $\epsilon$: private prediction error; $\eta$: other measured-displacement contributions (all degrees over 350 ms); $C$ here is a random displacement, not a covariance function; $R$: Pearson correlation of $X$ and $Y$ (dimensionless); $\chi$: shared fraction $\operatorname{Var}(C)/\operatorname{Var}(Y)$, dimensionless; $\widehat\chi$: weighted estimate of $\chi$, reported 0.82 ± 0.07; $N_m$: motor-neuron population size (count); covariance and variances have degrees² units. The ± value is propagated weighted estimation error, not between-animal spread.

20.symbols: $t$: time (s); $\ell$: positive sampling lag (s); $E(t)$: true horizontal eye angle; $E_{\rm obs}(t)$: measured angle; $\nu(t)$: position-reading error (all degrees); $\sigma_m^2$: variance of one position-reading error (degrees²); $M(\ell)$: true mean squared displacement $\mathbb E[(E(t+\ell)-E(t))^2]$ (degrees²); $M_{\rm obs}$: the corresponding measured MSD (degrees²). The displacement error contains two readings, hence $2\sigma_m^2$.

21.symbols: $E$: centered stationary eye angle (degrees); $t$, $u$, $\ell$: time, integration lag, and observation lag (s); $h(u)$: stable causal response kernel, with units degrees/(input-unit s); $\xi$: white input with an arbitrary fixed input unit $U$; $A$: white-input intensity defined by $\mathbb E[\xi(t)\xi(t')]=A\delta(t-t')$, units $U^2$ s; $C_E(\ell)$: output position covariance (degrees²); $M(\ell)$: output MSD (degrees²). Thus $h$ has degrees/($U$ s); it is not the spatial-input $h$ in place-field rows. $A$ is noise intensity, not the dimensionless visual-feedback gain used elsewhere.

22.symbols: $t$: time (s); $\ell$ and $s$: nonnegative time lags (s); $E$: filtered eye angle (degrees); $B$: accumulating Brownian position command (degrees); $\tau_f$: the teaching model's single eye-response time (s), written $\tau$ in the detailed chapter; $D$: temporal diffusion coefficient, with $\operatorname{Var}[B(t+\ell)-B(t)]=2D\ell$ (degrees²/s); $W$: standard Brownian process with increment variance $dt$ ($W$ has sqrt(s) units), not a synaptic weight; $v=\dot E$: velocity (degrees/s); $C_v(s)$: stationary velocity covariance (degrees²/s²); $M$: filtered-position MSD (degrees²). The 2012 synaptic $\tau$ and this $\tau_f$ describe different processes.

23.symbols: $N$: number of comparable integrator neurons (count); $\lambda$, $\lambda_0$: firing rate and typical mean firing rate (spikes/s); $E$: represented eye angle (degrees); $a=d\lambda/dE$: absolute tuning slope (spikes/(s degree)); $b=a/\lambda_0$: fractional tuning slope (1/degree); $J$: Poisson Fisher information per unit time about angle (1/(s degree²)); $\mathrm{CV}$: interspike-interval standard deviation divided by its mean (dimensionless); $\tau_s$: synaptic decay time (s); $D$: angle diffusion coefficient (degrees²/s). Here $a$ and $b$ are slopes, not the place firing-rate gain or a conditioned peak height. Printed paper $k_0$ is called position sensitivity but its absolute/fractional normalization is unclear.
23.paper_location: Guide Poisson/renewal scale comparison. Related paper expression: Ben-Shushan et al. (2022), main Eq. 1 and parameter discussion, PDF p. 6; sub-Poisson construction in Methods 'Sub-Poisson spike trains', PDF p. 11. The paper prints inverse lambda_0 dependence without clarifying the slope normalization.

23.status: Guide supporting scale estimate and paper Eq. 1 comparison; not an exact equation for the full saturating, sub-Poisson network.

24.symbols: $x$: spatial position (a scalar on a track or vector in $\mathbb R^d$, distance units); $d$: spatial dimension (1, 2, or 3), not diffusion; $h(x)$: fixed Gaussian input map in an input unit $U$; $\mu$: constant input mean ($U$); $\sigma_0$: input standard deviation ($U$); $h_{\rm th}$: absolute input threshold ($U$); $z=(h-\mu)/\sigma_0$: unit-variance normalized input (dimensionless); $q=(h_{\rm th}-\mu)/\sigma_0$: normalized threshold (dimensionless); $F$: firing rate (Hz); $a$: firing-rate gain for normalized excess (Hz); $C$: covariance of unnormalized input $h$ ($U^2$); $C''(0)$: second spatial derivative of covariance along a unit direction ($U^2$/distance²); $\ell_c$: local spatial scale (distance), written $\sigma$ in the detailed chapters; $z'$: spatial derivative (1/distance). The normalized covariance is $C/C(0)$, not $C$ itself. $q$ is unrelated to the 2012 Gaussian-noise intensity $q_n$. $[u]_+=\max(u,0)$ keeps positive input excess and sets negative excess to zero; $u$ is a dimensionless placeholder for $z-q$.
24.paper_location: Mainali et al. (2025), STAR Methods 'Model details', Eqs. 2–3, main PDF pp. 13–14; local spatial scale Eq. 4, main PDF p. 14. The guide makes the removable constant mean and rate gain explicit. Supplement Methods S1, PDF p. 9, defines the spatial Gaussian process.

24.status: Paper spatial Gaussian threshold model and local scale, with explicit guide normalization.

25.symbols: $x$,$y$: spatial positions (vectors in $\mathbb R^d$ with distance units); $i$: input-cell index; $u_i(x)$: fixed spatial firing profile of input cell $i$ (Hz); $W_i$: fixed random synaptic weight with zero mean (input-unit/Hz); $v_W=\operatorname{Var}(W_i)$: weight variance (input-unit²/Hz²); $h(x)$: summed input (input-unit); $C(x,y)$: unnormalized input covariance across choices of weights (input-unit²). $W_i$ is a random weight, not Brownian $W$; $u_i$ is a tuning profile, not a time lag. The Gaussian limit needs many active terms with no dominant input; dimensions and covariance depend on the fixed input profiles.

25.status: Paper supporting input-generation model; guide expands the covariance calculation and conditions for a Gaussian limit.

26.symbols: $q$: dimensionless threshold of normalized input $z$; $z$: zero-mean unit-variance spatial Gaussian map; $z'$: derivative along the track (1/distance); $\ell_c$: local distance scale, paper $\sigma$; $\nu_+(q)$: expected upcrossings per distance; $L$: track length (distance); $N_L$: number of connected active intervals intersecting [0,$L$], including clipped intervals (count); $Z$: standard normal scalar (dimensionless); $Q(q)=\Pr(Z>q)$: Gaussian upper-tail probability (dimensionless). Height density is per normalized-input unit, and mean positive slope has inverse-distance units.

27.symbols: $\mu_s$: stationary mean complete-field length; $\mu_g$: stationary mean complete-gap length; $\ell_c$: local spatial scale (all distance units); $q$: dimensionless normalized threshold; $\nu_+=e^{-q^2/2}/(2\pi\ell_c)$: upcrossing density (1/distance); $Q(q)$: standard normal upper-tail probability; $Q^{-1}$: inverse upper-tail function (both dimensionless). These means are per field or gap, not per occupied position; $\mu_s$ is not the input mean $\mu$ and is not a finite clipped-track ratio.

28.symbols: $N_L$: number of rare field locations on a track of length $L$; $N$: unconditioned field count (counts); $L$: track length; $G$: inactive gap length; $g$: chosen nonnegative gap cutoff (all distance units); $\nu_+$: rare-event/upcrossing density (1/distance); $\lambda$: unconditioned Poisson mean count (dimensionless), not a firing rate here; $q$: dimensionless normalized threshold. $\operatorname{Poisson}(\nu_+ L)$ is a count distribution. The exponential survival concerns large gaps in the rare-field limit; the conditioned mean excludes $N=0$ cells.

29.symbols: $d$: spatial dimension (1,2,3), not a temporal diffusion coefficient; $s$: random field size, a length/area/volume ($\mathrm{distance}^{d}$); $S$: nonnegative size cutoff with the same units; $q$: large positive dimensionless normalized threshold; $\ell_c$: local distance scale; $\epsilon$: normalized peak excess above $q$ (dimensionless); $U=q\epsilon$: scaled excess tending to a mean-one exponential variable (dimensionless); $r_*$: approximate field radius (distance), not a firing rate; $v_d$: volume of a unit-radius $d$ dimensional ball, dimensionless, $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=(2,\pi,4\pi/3)$; $\beta$: size-law coefficient (inverse distance²), so $\beta S^{2/d}$ is dimensionless. Each field is sampled once, not weighted by occupied volume.

30.symbols: $F_{\max}$: maximum firing rate in a field (Hz); $a$: gain converting normalized excess input into firing rate (Hz), not the eye tuning slope; $\epsilon$: peak normalized input minus threshold $q$ (dimensionless); $q$: large positive normalized threshold (dimensionless); $\ell_c$ and $r_*$: local scale and field radius (distance); $d$: spatial dimension; $s$: complete field length/area/volume ($\mathrm{distance}^{d}$); $v_d$: dimensionless unit-ball volume; $s^{1/d}$: a linear-size measure (distance). For a 1D full width, $v_1=2$.

31.symbols: $s$: random complete-field size ($\mathrm{distance}^{d}$); $d$: spatial dimension; $k$: nonnegative moment order (dimensionless), not an eye position coefficient; $\beta$: size-law coefficient ($\mathrm{distance}^{-2}$); $\mu_s=\mathbb E[s]$: mean size ($\mathrm{distance}^{d}$), not input mean; $u=\beta s^{2/d}$: dimensionless integration variable; $\Gamma$: gamma function, $\Gamma(t)=\int_0^\infty u^{t-1}e^{-u}\,du$ for $t>0$. Thus $\mathbb E[s^k]$ has $\mathrm{distance}^{dk}$ units. The field-size mean in this row is a limiting mean, unlike the exact 1D mean in P4.

32.symbols: $x_0$: point on a sampling line (position vector in $\mathbb R^d$, distance units); $\mathbf e$: fixed unit direction vector in $\mathbb R^d$ (dimensionless); $t$,$t'$: signed spatial coordinates along that line (distance), not times; $h(x)$: fixed Gaussian spatial input (input-unit); $h_{\rm line}(t)$: restriction of that input to the line (input-unit); $C(\Delta x)$: unnormalized stationary input covariance (input-unit²) as a function of vector displacement; $C_{\rm line}(t,t')$: restricted covariance (input-unit²); $\ell_c$: local distance scale; $d$: dimension of original map, distinct from dimension of the line or plane slice. $h$ here is spatial input, not an eye filter.

(2025), main Fig. 2C–D and H–J, PDF p. 5, and Results 'Statistics of place fields in two- and three-dimensional environments', PDF pp. 3,6; alternative spherical model and slice comparison Fig. S2, supplement PDF pp. 3–4. 33.symbols: $z$: dimensionless normalized spatial input; $x$: track coordinate (distance); $v=z'(x)>0$: normalized input slope at a typical upcrossing (1/distance); $\ell_c$: local spatial scale (distance); $p_{\uparrow}(v)$: probability density of upcrossing slope (distance units, reciprocal to $v$); $p_{z'}(v)$: ordinary spatial derivative density (distance units); $w$, if used for normalization: another positive slope variable (1/distance); $q$: dimensionless threshold; $a$: firing-rate gain (Hz); $av$: rate slope at a boundary (Hz/distance). This slope variable $v$ differs from eye velocity and from unit-ball volume $v_d$.

34.symbols: $q$: dimensionless normalized input threshold; $\ell_c$: local spatial scale (distance); $d$: box dimension, 1,2,3; $j$: dimension of contributing interior/face/edge, an integer 1 through $d$; $L$: box side length (distance); $\eta_j$: signed expected Euler-characteristic contribution per $j$ dimensional measure ($\mathrm{distance}^{-j}$), not positive field density; $\chi_d$: Euler characteristic of the active excursion set in the $d$ dimensional closed box (dimensionless signed count); $Q(q)$: standard Gaussian upper-tail probability. $\chi_d$ is unrelated to the eye variance fraction $\chi$, and $\eta_j$ is unrelated to eye measurement noise $\eta$. The final sum includes real boundaries; periodic boxes require other boundary terms.

35.symbols: $N$: number of connected active fields (count), not neuron number in this row; $q$: large positive normalized threshold (dimensionless); $d$: spatial dimension, not diffusion; $V$: environment length/area/volume ($\mathrm{distance}^{d}$); $\ell_c$: local spatial distance scale; $\chi_d$: Euler characteristic (dimensionless signed count), approximately $N$ only when components are simple isolated blobs. The expression is dimensionless overall and omits boundary contributions.
